item.title: Imo West ruling could cost Tinubu South-East votes, APC group warns
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — A pro-Tinubu group, Renewed Hope Foot Soldiers for Tinubu (RHFST), has warned that the Federal High Court’s ruling recognising Rochas Okorocha as the duly elected All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District could heighten political tensions in the South-East and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s support ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group’s National President, Hon. Gbenga Owojori, who raised the concern in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja, said the dispute had implications beyond the senatorial constituency, particularly for the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency. “The dispute over the Imo West ticket has consequences beyond the constituency. It has altered the political calculations surrounding the Senate presidency and raised concern that a leading South-East contender could be shut out of the contest before the next Senate is constituted,” the group said. It argued that Governor Hope Uzodimma, a former senator, should be allowed to pursue his political ambitions in accordance with established rules. According to the group, Uzodimma’s supporters consider him a credible contender for the Senate presidency, with backing from political leaders across party lines. The group also drew attention to allegations by critics that Senate President Godswill Akpabio had an interest in preventing Uzodimma from emerging as a potential rival, while former Rivers State Governor and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, was allegedly involved in efforts to pursue a legal challenge against the Imo governor. It said the allegations had been linked by critics to Akpabio’s previous support for Wike during his political disagreement with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The group further expressed concern over allegations that Wike may have influenced the court proceedings, citing claims by Uzodimma’s supporters that the FCT minister had repeatedly threatened to deal with the Imo governor. However, RHFST cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, insisting that the judgment should be assessed on its legal merits. “These are serious claims and should not be treated as established facts. The judgment must be assessed on its legal merits, and the statements attributed to Wike require clarification. Given the political consequences of the ruling, the public deserves confidence that no political pressure has influenced the judicial process,” it said. The group maintained that Uzodimma should be assessed on his political record, experience and support base, rather than being denied an opportunity to pursue his ambitions. It urged the APC to ensure transparency in its nomination processes and avoid actions that could be perceived as excluding candidates to protect the political interests of others. item.title: 2027: Presidency should remain in South until 2031 — BTO For PBAT
item.description: Group says move will strengthen national unity, political stability, democratic inclusiveness By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Director-General of BTO For PBAT ’27 Support Group, Ogbeni Adojutelegan Adesuyi Gideon, has said the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria until 2031 to promote equity, fairness and political balance. Adojutelegan said allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure would strengthen national unity, sustain democratic stability and give all geopolitical zones a sense of belonging. In a statement issued in Akure, he acknowledged that power rotation was not expressly provided for in the Constitution but argued that it remained an important political arrangement for sustaining national cohesion and strengthening democratic institutions. He said the issue should be approached with political maturity and a commitment to the stability of the federation. The group, which operates under the leadership of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said equitable political arrangements were essential to sustaining mutual trust and deepening democracy. Adojutelegan described the return of power to the South in 2023 as significant, arguing that allowing the region to complete eight years in 2031 would serve the interest of political balance. “The position of BTO For PBAT ’27 is clear and unequivocal: the presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria should remain in the South until 2031. “This position is not founded on sectional sentiment or regional antagonism. It is anchored on the fundamental principles of equity, fairness, justice and the need to sustain mutual understanding among the various geopolitical zones that constitute our great nation. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023. We believe that allowing the South to complete an eight-year presidential tenure, subject to the sovereign decision of Nigerians at the ballot box in 2027, would reinforce the spirit of fairness and political accommodation,” he said. He maintained that Nigeria’s democratic stability depended not only on constitutional provisions and elections but also on leaders’ willingness to uphold inclusion, balance and mutual respect. While acknowledging the constitutional right of every qualified Nigerian to contest elections, he urged political stakeholders to consider arrangements that would strengthen public confidence in the fairness of the political system. “The presidency is a national institution that belongs to all Nigerians. Its leadership must continue to reflect the aspirations, collective interests and democratic expectations of the federation. “We must recognise that political stability is strengthened when the various sections of the country believe that their interests are respected and their legitimate aspirations are fairly accommodated. “Our advocacy for the continuation of a southern presidency until 2031 is therefore a call for political fairness, national understanding and democratic consolidation,

The governors made the call during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East flagged off by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu at Okpara Square, Enugu, on Saturday. Speaking, the host governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, urged the people of the region to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the federal government’s economic reforms. “If I ask what future you want for your children, I’m sure you are seeing that future unfold gradually through the bold and courageous reforms of Mr. President. “It is through those reforms that enough money has been made available to all the states. Which is why in Enugu, when you look around you, you will see the Smart Green Schools, Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres, and numerous other projects and initiatives we have undertaken in just three years. This is happening because of the bold and courageous reforms of Mr. President and we know the job is not finished yet. We, the Igbos have gone to communities outside our zone to build businesses. And we also know how to build relationships. And that is being put to test. We are not a people that are ethnic bigots. We are a people that are strategic. “And that is why we must all come out in our numbers and support Mr. President to continue the good work. item.title: Remi Tinubu flags Off South-East women’s mega empowerment in Enugu
item.description: …Distributes empowerment materials, promises ₦200,000 business grants to 750 persons …As S’East governors throw their weight behind Tinubu’s re-election … Benjamin Kalu: Ndigbo not part of anybody’s one-term presidency arrangement, we deserve more Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Saturday flagged off the South-East Women Mega Empowerment and the All Progressives Congress’ Women Mobilisation Directorate’s campaign across the six geopolitical zones, saying the worst was over, as Nigeria was now stepping into prosperity flowing from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms. The rally, which climaxed with the distribution of empowerment materials such as sewing machines, food processors, electricity generating sets and popcorn machines to women drawn from the five states of the region to support their economic activities and small-scale businesses, also attracted the presence of women leaders and members of the party from Enugu, Abia, Ebonyi, Imo and Anambra states. Wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Nana Shettima, Governors Peter Mbah of Enugu State, Hope Uzodimma of Imo State and Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State, as well as the Deputy Governor of Anambra State, Dr. Onyekachukwu Ibezim, were also in attendance at the rally, which took place at Okpara Square, Enugu. Addressing the women, the First Lady, Senator Tinubu, conveyed President Tinubu’s goodwill message and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged by the economic challenges associated with the President’s reforms, insisting that the country was moving towards prosperity. She likened the process to childbirth, noting that although the period of labour could be painful, it ultimately led to delivery. “Mr. President said I should greet everyone. We have done reforms and we are now in prosperity. Don’t allow anyone to deceive you. The worst is over. We are stepping into prosperity,” she said. The First Lady described the empowerment initiative as an indication of the APC government’s commitment to translating its promises into practical interventions, noting that the party was combining political mobilisation with economic support. She expressed appreciation to the people of the South-East for their reception and support, recalling that she had visited the region several times since her husband’s assumption of office. Senator Tinubu also announced additional empowerment programmes for women and elderly persons in Enugu State, promising that on December 3, APC senatorial candidates would be provided with funds to empower 250 women each with ₦200,000 to establish businesses. She further announced an empowerment programme for 250 elderly persons scheduled for December 17, explaining that the beneficiaries must be aged 65 and above. According to her, each of the two interventions would cover 750 beneficiaries across the three senatorial districts of Enugu State. item.title: Immigration requirements hit African travellers hardest — IATA
item.description: By Dickson Omobola International Air Transport Association, IATA, has released the results of its 2026 Global Passenger Survey, GPS, revealing, among other findings, that immigration requirements have discouraged passengers from visiting certain destinations. IATA, which highlighted two other major trends in passenger behaviour and expectations, said travellers were embracing biometric identification to reduce repeated document checks and expressing strong interest in using digital passports for check-in and more personalised services during booking. The survey also found that artificial intelligence, AI, was changing how passengers planned their trips. From finding flights and comparing fares to discovering new destinations, passengers are increasingly incorporating AI into their travel planning. Speaking on the survey, IATA’s Senior Vice President, Operations, Safety and Security, Nick Careen, said: “Passengers are embracing technology to make travel easier. AI is becoming a mainstream travel planning tool, while biometrics and digital identity are creating a faster and more seamless airport experience. Yet many travellers continue to face barriers from complex immigration and visa processes. Governments can help by simplifying entry requirements, eliminating duplicate checks, and accelerating the issuance and acceptance of secure digital travel credentials.” According to the survey, nearly six in 10 passengers reported experiencing biometric identification at least once in the past 12 months, while satisfaction with the technology reached its highest level yet. Meanwhile, the survey showed that entry requirements were becoming a growing barrier to travel, even as passengers embraced technology. Immigration requirements had discouraged 43 per cent of passengers from visiting a destination, up from 33 per cent in 2025. Among passengers discouraged from travelling to a particular destination by geopolitical conflict, 72 per cent said safety was the main reason, while 13 per cent cited uncertainty over whether travel was possible. Of those deterred by immigration requirements, 53 per cent said the process was too complex. Privacy concerns and cost were less common reasons, accounting for 17 per cent each. IATA said African travellers were among the most satisfied with their travel experiences but were also the most likely to have been discouraged from visiting a destination by immigration requirements. item.title: Kidnapping horror in Edo:Woman, fellow kidnappers caught by CCTV to die
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu WHEN Governor Monday Okpebholo was sworn-in on November 12, 2024, he was said to have confided in a close aide that there were two things he detested and would not allow them fester in Edo State: Thugerry and cultism. Closely related to this was kidnapping and other violent crimes. To show that he was prepared to check these challenges, Okpebholo approached the state House of Assembly to strengthen the anti-cultism and anti-kidnapping laws which now provide that any building linked to kidnapping and cultism would be demolished while convicted kidnappers would face the death penalty. To make justice seamless and devoid of bureaucratic encumbrances, the governor approached the Chief Judge of the state to dedicate a court to the two issues of kidnapping and cultism. The test of the resolve of the governor against kidnappers and cultism happened on the morning of Sunday, June 14, 2026 when, in broad daylight at the popular Vegetable Market off Airport Road, dare-devil kidnappers, operating in a pepper red Lexus Jeep, alighted from their vehicle, shot the tyres of a parked Toyota Highlander to kidnap the occupant. The owner of the vehicle escaped but his wife was not lucky as the kidnappers went away with her. The video of the incident went viral on social media courtesy of a CCTV in a building opposite the area where the incident happened. With marching orders from Okpebholo and the Inspector General of Police, four suspects, including a female, were arrested a few days after in connection with the incident and they became the first test of the courts dedicated to kidnapping and cultism. Barely four months after the investigation and prosecution started, the four suspects, namely, Marvelous Isaac, Wisdom Michael, Rufus Emete Michael and Gift Rachael, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Defendants, were found guilty of the Vegetable Market kidnap and three others in different parts of the state and capital and also being members of a secret cult, and sentenced to death by hanging or by lethal injection. The charge sheet was marked CD/S/06C/2026 between the state and four Defendants. The judgment was delivered on September 29, 2026 by Justice A. T. Momodu. It took Momodu over three hours, 30 minutes to deliver his judgment during which he attributed the success recorded by the prosecution to the CCTV in the opposite building and advised that there should be a deliberate effort to install them in business areas, public and even homes. He said the prosecution called seven witnesses while seven exhibits tendered in the trial of kidnapping, armed robbery, illegal possession of firearms, conspiracy, and membership of a secret cult among others. “I wish to place on record my profound appreciation to the private citizen whose CCTV captured the scene of the Vegetable Market kidnapping incident”, the trial judge said. “That singular act of installing CCTV in his premises provided evidence which assisted the police in the detection and proof of the crime

item.title: Anti-party claims:Wike, Soludo, Adeleke fight back
item.description: •CSOs knock PDP, APGA, Accord leaders By Luminous Jannamike, Dickson Omobola, Henry Obeta & Esther Onyegbula The decision by some opposition governors to align with President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign has raised questions about party loyalty, political survival and the ability of opposition parties to present a united front ahead of the 2027 general election. At the centre of the unfolding political drama are the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP); Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA); and Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party. Findings by Sunday Vanguard showed that their political choices have placed their respective parties in a delicate position as they grapple with the implications of their members’ involvement in a campaign to return the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to power. Crisis Wike, a prominent PDP figure and former Rivers State governor, has maintained his support for Tinubu despite the protracted crisis within the PDP and his strained relationship with members of the party opposed to his position. Soludo, on his part, has had to navigate the implications of his political relationship with the President while remaining in APGA, a party with its own electoral ambitions and identity. Adeleke’s emergence under the Accord Party banner has also drawn attention to the political calculations surrounding his relationship with the Tinubu-led administration and the implications for his party. Although the circumstances surrounding the three politicians differ, their positions have triggered debate over whether opposition politicians can support the electoral ambitions of a rival party without undermining the platforms on which they built their political careers. Against the backdrop of the approaching 2027 elections, the development presents a test of the PDP, APGA and Accord Party’s capacity to manage internal disagreements, defend their political identities and determine the limits of acceptable conduct by their prominent members. It has also raised questions about the strength of party discipline in Nigeria, where political allegiances are frequently shaped by personal interests, strategic calculations and the search for relevance in the corridors of power. Also, many are unsure whether what the politicians have done amounts to anti-party activities. Constitution Accordingly, the constitutions of the affected parties, in various sections, spell out actions that could constitute anti-party activities. Specifically, Section 10(6) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Constitution provides that no member shall align with other parties or groups to undermine the party or any of its elected governments. item.title: Ebola scare in Adamawa: NCDC confirms negative tests
item.description: …Two suspected cases test negative after two rounds of laboratory tests By Chioma Obinna The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) last night said two suspected Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests, assuring Nigerians that the confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remains the only confirmed infection reported in the country. The agency said the two individuals, who presented with symptoms suggestive of Ebola in Yola, were isolated as public health authorities commenced investigations and appropriate response measures. In a press statement yesterday, the Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the report was received by the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) in the early hours of October 30, 2026. He said samples collected from the individuals were subjected to laboratory testing to establish the cause of their illness, adding that both tested negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing. “Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said. He clarified that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Adamawa, stressing that the index case previously confirmed in the FCT remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria. “At this juncture, I wish to commend the efforts of the Adamawa State’s Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive approach. NCDC will continue to provide appropriate technical support to the Adamawa State Government to strengthen their response operations,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of a Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja involving a traveller who arrived in Nigeria from Uganda. The emergence of the suspected cases in Adamawa had raised concerns about a possible spread of the disease, prompting the state and federal health authorities to activate investigation and precautionary measures. However, the negative laboratory results have ruled out Ebola infection in the two individuals, based on the tests reported by the NCDC. Idris urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about the situation. “We urge members of the public to remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information or speculation about the situation. The public is encouraged to obtain information from official government and public health communication channels,” he said. The NCDC director-general, however, emphasised the need for continued vigilance, noting that Ebola was a serious infectious disease requiring prompt identification, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures. item.title: I am no more your leader, Wike is: Fubara faces uncertain future after surrendering
item.description: By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt With dexterity and some sense of candor, he strode purposefully along the red carpet isle to the podium. His assigned role for the day was unambiguously defined: To unveil the Rainbow Coalition candidates for the 2027 general elections in Rivers State. But unknown to many, Governor Siminalayi Fubara had a special announcement to make. First, he took a brisk eye scan through the sea of heads at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, then announced: “I am no more your leader. Stop calling me ‘my leader, my leader’” The day was Tuesday, October 27, 2026, when a political group formed by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, organized a rally which drew participants from the 23 local government areas of the state. They converged on the Yakubu Gowon Stadium Port Harcourt to display which candidate from the six-member political parties that constitute the Rainbow Coalition for the coming elections. Fubara was tactically chosen to perform the unveiling and handover the flag of the All Progressives Congress, APC, to Hon Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, the anointed governorship candidate of Wike. Fubara did not only surrender his potential second term as a sitting governor to Chinda but also relinquished his role as the political leader of Rivers to Wike. The governor veered off the track of duty and handed down a stern warning, or so it seemed, to his organic supporters who stood by him in thick and thin during the dark moment of the political crisis in Rivers, telling them unreservedly that he was no more their leader. “Let me say something here so that it will always help us while we move forward”, he started. “I’m aware there are some issues where some persons who followed me when we had the crisis when you’re in your meeting you say ‘my leader, my leader’. “We are now in one house. And because we have one house, there is no issue about who is the leader. “I might be your oga (governor) but we have a common leader now. So, please, going forward, this issue of ‘my leader, my leader, my leader’, I want it resolved here and now.” There was a cumulus of silence at first, then a deafening applause. Governors as leaders Way back in January 2025, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through his Vice, Kasim Shettima, had declared that all APC governors were political leaders of the party in their states. The implication is that as the highest political position in the state, a governor is seen as a leader politically. Tinubu made this known during the defection of Governor Agbu Kefas of Taraba State from PDP to APC. That pronouncement also covered Fubara the moment he defected from the same PDP to APC on December 9, 2025 and picked the 001 registration number of the ruling party. item.title: 77 days to polls:Parties clash over INEC’s preparations
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Luminous Jannamike & Omeiza Ajayi With barely 77 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns over the preparedness of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, have become disturbing, especially following the discovery of artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the commission’s preliminary voters’ register. The development has raised fresh questions about the integrity of the electoral database, the effectiveness of INEC’s internal monitoring mechanisms and the commission’s capacity to conduct elections that would command public confidence. Accordingly, the worries have been compounded by complaints about other irregularities in the preliminary register, including questionable names, addresses, genders and photographs. Although INEC has acknowledged the problem and promised to clean up the register before the final version is released on December 15, 2026, the development has exposed vulnerabilities in the registration process. The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed that some registration officers allegedly used their official login credentials to introduce irregular entries into the database. He, however, assured Nigerians that the commission had identified those responsible and was taking steps to address the situation. Registered voters INEC’s preliminary register, uploaded on October 26, 2026, contains over 103.4 million registered voters. Bayode explained that the figure reflected the more than 93 million voters recorded in the 2023 register and additional registrations from the continuous voter registration exercise ahead of the forthcoming elections. He said INEC was deploying technology to address the identified shortcomings, adding that its Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, had detected several questionable photographs before the preliminary register was released. Against this backdrop, Sunday Vanguard spoke with officials of political parties to ascertain their assessment of INEC’s preparations, the implications of the AI-generated images and what the commission needs to do to guarantee credible elections. While some parties expressed reservations about the development and called for urgent measures to restore public confidence, others maintained that the discovery should not be exaggerated, insisting that INEC had sufficient time to address the identified problems. The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, said the situation had moved beyond speculation following the commission’s admission that irregularities had occurred. item.title: Fasoranti’s death: Rumbling in Yorubaland, a new Afenifere may emerge
item.description: Old guard moves to form ‘Afenifere Independent’ Oba Olaitan calls for truce Forceful acquisition of pan-Yoruba group is dead on arrival —Ex-spokesman ‘Without Adebanjo’s camp support for Peter Obi, Tinubu may not have been president’ By Dapo Akinrefon The leadership crisis within the pan-Yoruba socio-political organization, Afenifere, may be far from being over. This is as a result of a factional camp asking other factions to unite behind the leadership of Oba Oladipo Olaitan. But while most of the Fasoranti camp vowed to resist such a move, some of the old guards, it was gathered, plan to form another Afenifere. Most of them, who belong to various factions, disagree over cultural succession norms and the potential emergence of a break-away Yoruba group. A source told Sunday Vanguard that discussions are ongoing to jettison both camps and start on a clean slate. Multiple sources said there is a need to resuscitate Afenifere and give the Yoruba race a formidable platform. A credible source informed Vanguard that while some members of the group are making moves to throw up what they called Afenifere Independent, the Akure camp is gearing up to name a former governor as Fasoranti’s successor. The source said: “One thing I know is that the Akure camp will not approve that Oba Oladipo Olaitan emerges as Afenifere leader. I know who they are planning to name as Fasoranti’s successor. He is a former governor. The two camps cannot be united as it is and that is why some of us having made up our mind to come up with Afenifere Independent.” Last week, following the death of Pa Reuben Fasoranti, the Oba Olaitan camp formally announced the consolidation of its collective leadership under his (Olaitan’s) stewardship. It said the transition was a tribute to Fasoranti’s legacy and a step towards promoting unity and defending Yoruba socio-political interests. The factional National Publicity Secretary and Secretary-General, Prince Justice Faloye and Alade Rotimi-John respectively, said Olaitan had demonstrated sincerity of purpose and the capacity to champion the group’s interests while promoting national unity. The statement read: “The modern history of the Yoruba people and the political evolution of Nigeria bear the indelible mark of Fasoranti. As a patriarch of principles, Pa Fasoranti carried the sacred torch of Afenifere with unyielding grace, following in the visionary footsteps of Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Senator Abraham Adesanya. Through seasons of national uncertainty, he stood as a steadfast moral compass, a relentless advocate for true federalism, equity, fairness and the progressive advancement of his people. His leadership anchored the Yoruba nation in wisdom, courage and an unshakeable commitment to justice and fair play.” In their defence, they were of the view that the consolidation of the great legacy now rests upon Oba Oladipo Olaitan, while they insisted that the time for division is over. item.title: Gada launches Sokoto East Senate campaign, receives defectors
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Former Senator Abubakar Umar Gada has declared the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) ready to reclaim political power in Sokoto State in 2027, following the defection of members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the party. Gada made the declaration on Saturday in Gwadabawa during the flag-off of his campaign for the Sokoto East Senatorial District seat, where he received the defectors and urged party supporters to mobilise ahead of the 2027 general elections. The former senator expressed confidence in the PDP’s prospects, describing Sokoto East as a traditional stronghold of the party despite its recent electoral setbacks. According to him, the PDP’s past electoral performance in the district provided a foundation for its anticipated comeback, adding that the party’s immediate task was to restore the confidence and determination of its supporters. “ SOKOTO East is traditionally a PDP zone. Past performance data and records have shown that. So, it is just to awaken them and bring back their self-consciousness, determination and readiness to take over,” Gada said. He maintained that his previous tenure in the Senate had equipped him with the experience and legislative accomplishments required to represent the district effectively. Gada said his record in the National Assembly distinguished him from other contenders seeking the seat. “I do not want to sound immodest, but I am always proud of my performance the last time I was in the Senate. People have recently made efforts, and I think they have done a lot, but compared to what we achieved at the time, it was absolutely incredible,” he said. Addressing the security and poverty challenges confronting communities in Sokoto East, Gada called for deliberate government intervention, strategic deployment of resources and increased federal attention to areas facing urgent developmental needs. He said the electorate deserved leadership capable of responding to insecurity, economic hardship and inadequate development, stressing that sustained government commitment was necessary to improve the living conditions of vulnerable communities. The PDP candidate also urged voters to defend their electoral rights and remain vigilant during the 2027 general elections, describing the ballot as a powerful instrument for determining their political future. “They are the power. Their votes are their guns and arsenals. Their voice is their weapon of battle. They should respect and understand that this is their God-given right,” he said. He warned that the consequences of electing unsuitable leaders could extend beyond the immediate electoral cycle, urging residents to make informed decisions based on their long-term interests and the future of their communities. item.title: MASUSUKA: Shocking assassination of outspoken cleric
item.description: •His brush with the Katsina government •Other clerics also killed By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The assassination of Islamic cleric Sheikh Yahaya Masusuka in Katsina State has rekindled concerns over the safety of religious scholars in Northern Nigeria, bringing back painful memories of previous killings that shocked Muslim communities and raised questions about the protection of outspoken religious figures. Masusuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, were shot dead on Monday, October 26, 2026, by armed men who arrived on a motorcycle outside the cleric’s residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State. The circumstances surrounding the attack remain unclear, including the identities of the gunmen and their motive. However, the killing has drawn attention to a sad history of assassinations involving prominent Islamic scholars in the North. Masusuka was known for his Qur’an-centred teachings, particularly his position that the Qur’an should be followed without reliance on Hadith traditions. His views generated disagreements with some Islamic scholars and attracted considerable attention on social media. Three decades He had reportedly spent more than three decades preaching Islam and studied at various institutions, including Al-Azhar University in Egypt. In November 2025, the Katsina State government summoned him following complaints about some of his teachings. The matter was referred to the Katsina Emirate Council for discussions, while Governor Dikko Radda directed him to respond to the allegations before a committee of Islamic scholars. His Secretary, Dr Mustapha Haruna, in an interview, also disclosed that the cleric had previously been arrested and spent some months in a correctional facility. The authorities have also received complaints from Masusuka that members of an Islamic sect were insulting him and threatening to attack him. Beyond preaching, Masusuka had established Qur’an TV/Radio and Masusuka International School in Dutsin-Ma, with the aim of combining Qur’anic and conventional education. He also advocated peaceful coexistence between Muslims and Christians and had received a Peace Ambassador award in June 2025. Killings, questions His death has now raised fresh questions about whether religious leaders facing threats receive adequate protection and whether disagreements over religious teachings are being addressed through peaceful and lawful means. Masusuka’s assassination relives the killing of Sheikh Ja’afar Mahmoud Adam, one of Nigeria’s most influential Islamic scholars, who was shot dead on April 13, 2007, while leading the early morning Fajr prayer at his mosque in the Gadon Kaya area of Kano. Sheikh Ja’afar commanded a large following among Sunni Muslims. He was also known for criticising extremist ideologies associated with Boko Haram. His killing shocked the Muslim community and raised questions about the security of religious scholars whose teachings and public engagements attracted both admiration and controversy.

item.title: 2027: Abejide seeks Kano non-indigenes’ support for APC
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf A member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Leke Abejide, has urged Yoruba people and other non-indigenous communities in Kano State to unite and mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Abejide, who represents Yagba West, Yagba East and Mopa-Muro Federal Constituency of Kogi State, made the appeal on Saturday at the 2026/2027 Kano State Empowerment Programme organised by the Leke Abejide Foundation. The lawmaker said he was concerned that Tinubu secured just over 500,000 votes across Kano’s 44 local government areas in the 2023 presidential election, despite the large population of Yoruba people and other non-indigenous communities in the state. Describing himself as the Asiwaju of Yoruba people in Kano, Abejide challenged the communities to organise themselves and mobilise support from polling units to wards and local government areas. “I want our people to unite and bring their votes together to show solidarity with President Tinubu. We must work together to support him, Governor Abba Yusuf and all APC candidates in the 2027 elections,” he said. Abejide also disclosed that the foundation was selecting coordinators from among women and widows benefiting from the empowerment programme to monitor and protect votes across polling units in Kano. He promised to return with a bigger empowerment programme if the beneficiaries continued to support his initiative, stressing that the intervention was not a one-off exercise. “What we are doing today will continue. Our aim is to help people build successful businesses and become millionaires and even billionaires in the future,” he said. Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, also urged non-indigenes in Kano to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections. Bello called on the communities to increase their support for the President, saying votes from non-indigenes in the state should rise significantly. “We must do better this time. I believe the votes from non-indigenes in Kano for the President should not be less than two million,” he said. He also urged the communities to support all APC candidates contesting for seats in the Senate, House of Representatives and State Houses of Assembly. Bello commended the Federal Government’s road projects, particularly the Kano-Abuja highway, describing them as evidence of Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructure development. He also praised the Kano State Government for what he described as positive changes in the state. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, who also attended the programme, urged members of the National Assembly to emulate Abejide by extending support to their communities and other Nigerians, irrespective of ethnic or religious differences. item.title: Eguavoen, CAF instructors at war over courses
item.description: Nigerian CAF instructors are up in arms against the NFF technical director, Austin Eguavoen over what they claimed as “unprofessional manner” he has been conducting a series of CAF D courses across the country. A majority of the 29 CAF instructors in Nigeria alleged that they have been sidelined from these courses and instead Eguavoen has been conducting the courses in Bayelsa, Edo, Delta, Ogun and Osun States with only Terry Eguaoje and one uncertified person. “W h a t Eguavoen is doing is very unprofessional,” one of the CAF instructors fired. “He has made the rest of us redundant even though we all are qualified to be part of these courses. “Instead, he is going around the country with only Dr Terry (Eguaoje) and one Fatai Akanji, who is not qualified to deliver papers at such courses. “Just how unprofessional can you be?” “These courses could be done across the country at the same time with some of us also being part of them,” added another CAF instructor. The tension between the instructors and Eguavoen has now reached a head that NIS DG Philip Shuaibu has waded into the crisis. This comes as a time that Eguavoen is seeking to stay on as NFF technical director following the expiration of his contract. item.title: Normalisation C’ttee: Recommended members fail FIFA integrity test
item.description: The Normalisation Committee to spearhead major reform in Nigerian football has yet to be announced because several of the committee members recommended did not scale the FIFA integrity test. The NFF announced in an official statement on October 22 that world football governing body FIFA have approved a Normalisation Committee to reorganise football in the country following the resignation of the NFF executive committee led by Ibrahim Gusau. The statement pointed out that the committee members will be jointly appointed by FIFA and CAF. Since then not much has been reported on this development. A top source has now informed that the delay in the announcement of this committee has been held back because several of the proposed members did not pass the integrity test conducted by FIFA. “Some of those recommended for the committee did not pass the FIFA test, that is partly why the committee is not yet in place, ” a top source said. “However, I wouldn’t want to give out the names of those who did not scale through.” It was further gathered that the committee will have between seven and nine members with strong indications that there could be as many as two non-Nigerians on it. Meanwhile, a former NFF general secretary as well as a one-time highly influential NFF executive committee member are among those lobbying to head the Normalisation Committee. The committee will be expected to round up by May 31, 2027. The post Normalisation C’ttee: Recommended members fail FIFA integrity test appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) Dortmund thought they had taken the lead with 35 minutes gone as Jobe Bellingham scored from close range, but VAR overturned the goal for offside. Bayern made Dortmund pay immediately when Konrad Laimer pounced on a poor Felix Nmecha pass and charged upfield to score. Bayern were better after the break and a Nmecha handball brought Kane to the spot, but the England captain rifled his shot against the crossbar. item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use. item.title: Man City Stunned In 0-1 Home Loss To Brighton
item.description: Manchester City suffered a second straight Premier League defeat at the hands of Brighton with a 1-0 win as the Seagulls went close within two points of the leaders on Saturday. Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title. The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials. Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday. Brighton’s French midfielder Georginio Rutter is put under pressure by Manchester City’s Portuguese midfielder Matheus Nunes (L) and Manchester City’s English midfielder #05 Elliot Anderson (R) during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead. Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time. Brighton’s German head coach Fabian Hurzeler reacts after the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side netting late on. City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. Manchester City’s Norwegian striker Erling Haaland reacts following the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Brighton and Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld, they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight. Defeat for Maresca’s men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday. Man Utd Self-Implode Meanwhile, City’s neighbours Manchester United recorded their nine-game winless run, their longest without victory for 38 years, after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first-half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period. item.title: Africa’s First Ever Youth Olympics Open In Senegal
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, opened Saturday in the Senegalese capital, marking an historic moment for the continent. Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are omnipresent across Dakar, which is hosting nearly 2,700 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world. The event will see the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the young athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events. “Today it’s not just a nation that is welcoming the Youth Olympic Games; it’s an entire continent that is opening its arms”, Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told a sport and development summit Saturday ahead of the Games’ opening ceremony. Senegal’s Influencer and TikToker Khaby Lame carries the Youth Olympic Flame on the eve of the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar on October 30, 2026. Photo by PATRICK MEINHARDT / AFP The Games will not only celebrate champions but also “our collective capacity to transform sport into an economic and social engine”, he said, emphasising that 130 years of Olympic history had passed before the Olympic flame ever landed on African soil. Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations. Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly, located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events. The Games are “showing the world our capacity (as Africa), a capacity that sometimes is underestimated”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Saturday during the summit. According to Coventry, the opening ceremony will be televised live in more than 30 countries, with every African nation having committed to showing the Games live, she said. Sports Culture An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games. A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event. The West African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene. Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or on weekends on the beach or in village squares. And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise. While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics has struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal. Mexican athletes arrive with their suitcases at the Youth Olympic Village in Diamniadio, on October 29, 2026.
